Hi Evelyn,

Hope you’re well — quick ask from our side as we scope the next quarter. We’re trying to centralize payment windows across our EU entities and would like to propose: 1) move our billing cadence with Redwood from Net30 to Net45, and 2) add an optional early-payment discount (1% if paid within 10 days) as an alternative to standard terms.

Two items I want to flag:
- VAT handling: for some of our EU subsidiaries we expect reverse-charge treatment, but we’ll need Redwood to confirm what evidence is required.
- Credit ceiling: we’d like to avoid extra deposits; would Redwood consider a modest swingline (temporary +$100k credit buffer) tied to the signed SOW?

Attaching a short spreadsheet with our expected payment cadence for the next 6 months (VAT-qa.xlsx).

Can you let me know if this is something Redwood finance can support? Happy to jump on a 20-min call with Marissa/finance.

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of Finance, Veltica Labs

Hi Oliver — thanks for the brief. I reviewed the attachment and sketched two workable proposals that balance cashflow and credit risk:

Option A — Net45 (standard)
- Terms: Net45 for all invoices going forward
- Credit: no additional deposit required; existing credit limit holds (EUR 250k)
- Early-pay discount: 1.0% if paid within 10 days (applies to invoices < EUR 100k or to första tranche of each invoice)
- Approval: Finance manager (me) can approve immediately; legal keeps MSA unchanged

Option B — Net45 + swingline (graduated)
- Terms: Net45
- Swingline: temporary +EUR 100k credit buffer for 90 days, subject to: signed SOW addendum and short health check (usage trend and billing age < 60 days)
- Early-pay discount: 0.75% for invoices paid within 15 days (lower to offset credit exposure)
- Approval: requires VP finance sign-off; canonical DocuSign addendum needed

VAT / evidence: for reverse-charge we need all of the following before we change VAT handling:
- Registered VAT number for the billing entity
- Signed SOW that states the billing entity and reverse-charge intent
- Copy of the invoice recipient registration (company registry extract or equivalent)

I attached a one-page proposed payment schedule (proposed-payment-schedule-v2.pdf) and I can prepare a short checklist to make this operational.

If you’re comfortable, we can pilot Option A immediately and activate Option B after DocuSign addendum. Which would you prefer?

Cheers,
Marissa
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-payment-schedule-v2.pdf]

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. Two quick responses from our side:
1) We prefer Option B (Net45 + swingline) since it gives us runway for the next quarter while we centralize collections. We can sign an addendum; could you send the DocuSign template?
2) VAT evidence: Oliver (me) will upload the VAT number and a company registry extract into the DocuSign/HubSpot attachment area.

One operational ask: can the swingline buffer be used selectively (not to exceed invoice >60 days overdue)? In practice we’ll use it only for normal timing differences — not to defer payment beyond the Net45 window.

If you can route the addendum to the signer (our CFO is Helena Park), we’ll aim to return it within 72 hours.

Best,
Oliver
